citations.review_text:
Still experiencing crashes after all the updates. When it runs well, the game is great! But, often it tends to crash in the middle of a hunt. 

Maybe after they fully patch the game itll be worth a positive review.
I want to like this game but it constantly crashed every 5-30 min of playtime. Everything on the internet does not work to fix the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story progression as heavily linear and interrupted by long, unskippable cutscenes or forced walking segments.

citations.review_text:
I have been playing Monster Hunter for years, and I consider the combat in Monster Hunter Wilds the best I have experienced. It is quicker, more dynamic, and you have more options. I love it! My sword and board builds are still fun, there are the traditional combos to use with a few new ones, and the ability to switch to a backup weapon mid-combat really helps open up builds.

That being said, the game tries too hard to make the plot front and center. The plot takes its self too seriously and requires too many unskippable riding scenes where they throw dialogue at me that I really don't care about. I don't mean to be rude, but I generally don't play Monster Hunter games for the plot. I like enough plot to string the hunts together and help create a fun world, but I really don't need/want them trying this hard to make me care about random NPCs. It isn't working, and it makes the game feel a wee bit tedious at times.

I will probably keep playing the game because I paid for it.  But honestly, the story sucks AND it takes forever.
I feel like I am stuck watching a shitty movie most of the time, and then the monster hunting is just added on.
Rise and World at least gave you autonomy when finding and fighting monsters.  This one, you are put on rails and have to sit through 10 mins of dialogue (before AND after a hunt) for a 10 min monster fight.
The game would be way better if all the NPCs were removed.
EDIT:  I actually timed how long it took from the end screen of one hunt to the first hit on the next hunt without skipping anything, and doing no inventory mangagement or cooking.  Just the cutscenes and forced auto walk.  It was 20 mins, 20 seconds.  The hunt before and after were 7:49 and 10:13.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience difficulty or frustration when trying to set up and connect with friends for cooperative play.

citations.review_text:
I quite literally had to build a new PC to play this. This game was at the very top of the list of games I wanted to play when I got an all team red PC. You can see my previous Hyprland build on other reviews of mine. When i had an Intel/Nvidia build...

This game was exploding polygons and I could see literally nothing. It was basically eye-molestation repeatedly. When I moved it would explode in all sorts of vertices and would run around 6-8FPS. 

Now though? With my top of the line AMD setup I get well over 150FPS most of the time with the high end texture pack applied and with Freesync on the 27" OLED its INCREDIBLE. 

This game ROCKS. It plays incredibly well, feels like a true monster hunter, and scratches that itch. 

The only real drawback that I have seen so far is setting up friends, connecting with friends (link), and all of that is a huge PiTA the first time you set it up. But once you get that and triggering HDR on Hyprland Linux (its kind of a pain too), its fantastic. 

So far, 9/10. Having an absolute blast and highly recommend this game!!

Deck User here. 
The game is great, there are many things I like about it. The cast of characters is much better than World and a lot of the tediousness was removed from the game. The tracking was automated for the most part, I personally do not mind this but I can understand the people who say that it's part of the IP's essence and the game feels more shallow the way it is now.

The Verified Status unfortunately is a massive lie and the most drunk checkmark on any game I've seen on Steam. Wilds requires a lot of manual graphic and performance adjustments and nothing other than force-running it on Proton Experimental would even start it for me but then the single player worked fine aside from some smaller hiccups in the wide open areas. 
Now here is the big catch and what ultimately downvotes this for me. If you are seeking to play with friends you'll have a rough time here because the connection keeps breaking often directly after connecting and good luck trying a hunt with a friend without the Deck user dropping from it midway. And the worst part of World, having to watch cutscenes separately in order to play the same Hunt, somehow made it into this game despite World also having instances where it was possible to join the same hunt at once. 
I played World (also on Deck) with a good mate together and we played the entire game Co-Op. Ran smoothly, hardly ever broke or dropped frames and looked far better to boot. I really am lost for words with how bad the online performance of Wilds is in comparison. The two games are night and day.

I really hope that the upcoming DLC acts as the saving grace for this problem. I am willing to flip the thumb if it does. My friend and I will likely have to abandon our playthrough if it doesn't get better.

claims.claim: Reviewers find the game's early difficulty to be too easy or hand-holding.

citations.review_text: IDK why I bought this. Ive owned the other game forever and only have like 10 hrs in it. For whatever reason im having fun. I am growing in concern in regards to this games difficulty. I play solo and at 14hrs in ive yet to be killed or even come close to failing anything. I hope im still just in the hand holding section. If it stays this easy then the gameplay loop needs to get a little more enticing if im gonna keep a positive review.

I can't stand how hand-holdy this game is. I just want to go out and kill monsters, but I have to follow these random, poorly written, boring NPCs around for hours.

If you try to explore on your own, the game prevents you from doing so and forces you to get back to the story. I want to hunt monsters, not talk to all these random fucks. 

They forgot that the best way to reveal a world is to show, not tell. Game is auto pilot and they treat you like a baby.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that multiplayer and connecting to servers is plagued by issues, making it difficult or impossible to play with others online.

citations.review_text: I still cannot connect to the server. I cannot do multi player which is insane.

The game is great and very fun, I played World a ton and enjoy this game. The only reason for my review is because this game has a massive connection issue and after troubleshooting every single possible fix, nothing changed and I can no longer play with friends or even stay connected to the servers for more than a few minutes. Capcom refuses to acknowledge this issue and blames users instead of looking into the problem. I have no issues with any other game except this. So unless they fix it and I can play the game online, I will leave my review as is and will certainly not be buying the expansion or even bothering to play the game at this point.

Sadly I can't recommend this game out of principle. Game was launched in a horrible state and they took over a year to fix it and even then the game is still frustrating to play (The multiplayer experience in particular. Good Lord the user interface to join a friend's session is a nightmare). Clearly the publisher just wanted to rush out a game to pad sales numbers and didn't care about the PC players. It doesn't matter how good the game is now, I can't recommend a game that was launched in a mess and fixed later.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the user interface and menus are poorly designed and frustrating to navigate.

citations.review_text:
[h3][b]Positives[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Engaging combat
[*]Beautiful music, both ambience and in combat
[*]Gorgeous open world with plenty of variation.
[*]Lots of build variety and complex mechanics
[*]Adorable cat companion
[*]Cooking animation makes my mouth water every time
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Negatives[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Awful user interface, but it's a series staple at this point
[*]The story is a bit simplistic, and it feels more like a vehicle to just drip-feed new monsters to the environment, not to explore concepts or say something important
[*]A lot of gameplay mechanics are not properly explained and can bite you in the ass during combat
[*]Arena fights are honestly really bad
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Notes[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Occasional performance dips to 60 FPS during bad weather and low textures on various characters
[*]Wonky free-roam multiplayer implementation
[*]controls take a lot of time to get used to, but will click eventually
[*]Many many hours of content
[*]Very unapologetic product placement of various Japanese products and other games
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Full Review[/b][/h3]

Monster Hunter Wilds is not my first Monster Hunter game (that would be World), but it is the first one I've played to completion of the main questline. I played it a little bit back when it released, but stopped shortly after getting access to the second biome. I got the itch to play it again about a month ago, and decided to stick with it until the end. And with that, I believe I have a firm enough grasp of the game to make a review of it.

Wilds is obviously a divisive entry into the Monster Hunter series (just look at the Steam Review score), but I think that is mostly because of the performance issues it has had. That said, the game has more problems than its performance, but nothing that can't be ignored or at least gotten used to. The story isn't much to write home about, and mere serves as a vehicle to introduce new biomes, mechanics and monsters, a…

The game is okay, but out of all the 1000s of hours in the games in the series I've played (everything after 3,) it's my least played and least favorite, it comes down to design. I think the "QOL" went way too far and took out most anything you would have had to use brainpower over, things to earn or keep track of:  You don't hunt or learn the monsters anymore, you don't really explore the world or notice any details, your self-driving mount takes you to monsters, and frustratingly, the game's default settings does it automatically like it's pulling you along on a leash. You no longer look for materials, or even AT them, you click a button like a quick-time event when you see a prompt pop up to gather from afar and get flooded with mats. It feels like the game is begging me not to explore or engage with the world they crafted.
 
I also found the story quests abhorrently boring, way too easy (which is a lot of hours of boring to get to challenging content) and I felt basically no reason to prepare or use any items except the occasional potion. There were no tough monsters that felt like a wall to my progress that I felt I had to learn and think about. It's a fundamentally brain-off experience.

The UI is atrocious. Using the multiplayer features are especially weird and confusing. This is the place that needed the QOL and polish, not the gameplay.

At least the combat is fun, though I found it less challenging and way more forgiving, leading to me zoning out while playing it. I worry that that every entry going forward is going to have this dumbed down hollow experience where you don't engage with the world at all.  I think World was a way better game and struck a good balance between old and new.

I hope the DLC will be fun, but I don't think they can or will go back on any of the stuff that aggravates me about this game.

Bonk big monsters, game looks beautiful and is very fun.
Wish UI was a bit bettter tho, especially menu and stuff but it is what it is.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as overly easy with a lack of challenge compared to previous entries in the series.

citations.review_text:
3/10
This game is trying to be a movie but the storyline is very mediocre. Other Monster Hunter games also lack impressive story but this game keeps trying to force attention to the story which makes it a far more glaring flaw. Either put effort/competence into writing a proper story or keep it out of view. 
The game kind of just plays itself through a lot of parts while you are forced to watch the character ride around on the Seikret (a horse-bird mount thing) and listen to boring, over-dramatic "blah" dialogue.
The game is mechanically unchallenging. There is no need to engage in strategy, learn monster weaknesses, experiment with different weapon types, etc. You don't even need to upgrade your armor throughout the whole game because the difficulty is so low. It feels like a never-ending tutorial that never turns into a proper game.
This would be a good game for 8-year-olds but the target audience is older, so it's a major miss. 

Redeeming factors: Good monster designs and nice cinematics.
Also the necessary PC specs are actually much lower than recommended.

The game absolutely works fine on older computers, but the automatic settings are terrible. You need to go into the settings and turn off a bunch of "features" that are destroying the performance/visuals. After you play around with the settings, you can get it looking and running quite nicely even on old computers (only a GTX 1070 and it runs fine and looks at least as good as MH World). If you don't change the default settings, it does look horrible (like a blurry mess made out of burlap sacks) and is unstable. There are annoying nag popups that can never be dismissed if your PC lacks the (unnecessary) recommended hardware. The problem is just the default settings.

**This Review should be a "mixed" but I cant do that, so it gets a Negative from me**

[b] If you are looking for a more chill Monsterhunter experience, with first time players to the Genre; This is the game for you![/b]



Wilds is a fine game. Nothing special game breaking wise. Some really good Improvement on the movement and weapons! Some nice QOL as well, and super pretty world and a cute mount!
The game is an easy game for new people to enter and learn. 
If you want a challange tho, play Worlds and prepared to be humbled!

Besides that, What can I say that hasnt been said?
Besides performance which is okayish now. At least for med-high end, the game is just kind of boring...
In Worlds you would sink 100s even 1000s of hours into one character because of all the content, the monsters, quests and the fighting.
Here I have spent roughl 65hrs in this game, AND I HAVE 2 CHARACTERS COMPLETED! 
So that should tell you what kind of content awaits you.

Some fights took 30min. in Worlds because the monster was that tough!
In wilds, the longest i have ever fought solo, was 12min. And I didnt even break a sweat. It felt super easy, and yet at the same time, when the monster was dead it was a "ok, nice" feeling.
I remember in worlds, I would stand up and scream when I first killed Lunastra Solo in her Mission. That fight was tough as hell for me back then!

But like I said; Its a super pretty and easy game for people that are new to the Series, or people that usualy struggle with these types of games. A good game to learn mechanics and stuff.

The UI is atrocious. Using the multiplayer features are especially weird and confusing. This is the place that needed the QOL and polish, not the gameplay.

At least the combat is fun, though I found it less challenging and way more forgiving, leading to me zoning out while playing it. I worry that that every entry going forward is going to have this dumbed down hollow experience where you don't engage with the world at all.  I think World was a way better game and struck a good balance between old and new.

I hope the DLC will be fun, but I don't think they can or will go back on any of the stuff that aggravates me about this game.

Wilds is a game made for game journalists.

This game marks a step forward for the series in terms of technology, narrative, characterization, and battle dynamics. However, it fundamentally loses sight of what makes the Monster Hunter formula compelling on too many fronts.

Battles are incredible to behold. The suite of new and improved options, animations, and dynamic reactions as the hunter and monster battle look and feel amazing. Clashing with monsters with your shield or guarding against breath weapons, offsetting them with mighty blows, or dashing across the length of their spines with a flurry of attacks are all really awesome to see. But you quickly realize that the game has completely abandoned anything resembling what made Monster Hunter fun: there is no challenge here whatsoever.

The reality that begins to dawn on you as you play is that this is a complete power fantasy rather than a struggle against monsters. Massive explosions that reverberate and overwhelm the senses with their awe deal meaningless amounts of damage or can be simply avoided. Half the time you can plant yourself beneath a monster and attack it for 30+ seconds while it randomly attacks at nothing. The most powerful and intimidating attacks with the greatest visual spectacle should instill FEAR and DANGER. Instead, they mean nothing.

The mismatch between visual awe and actual game difficulty kills any sense of investment. 

This game suffers immensely from AAA disease: you frequently find yourself being literally forced to walk a glowing path, redirected by invisible walls and the like, or are just as often encouraged to let your mount auto-navigate to your hunt location. These elements add up to create a cheap and meaningless experience. Health, status effects, monster information, sharpening, and trapping are all pseudo-automated or made trivial by the amount of assistance you receive. The result is that no victory feels earned or difficult. My only deaths came from, ironically, this …

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the endgame gear upgrade and crafting system as relying heavily on RNG and random rolls.

citations.review_text:
Worst endgame grind of the whole franchise combined with a game with no difficulty roadblocks (unless you try to solo Omega, the only hard monster in the game, and it's from a Final Fantasy Colab, just like Behemoth in World but worse).
Decorations I am ok with, but RNG Talismans and RNG Weapon Crafting? Fuck that, give me back killing monsters and making weapons out of them to get stronger, not some "here is a futuristic ass weapon bullshit from a civilization that was wiped eons ago that we invented to make the endgame bloated" (talking about endgame weapons here, you cannot use monster weapons and the game does not have monster weapons past the campaign, you have to farm parts of broken ancient weapons to make anything that is worth using).

I am a Warframe player with over 4.4k hours, I am used to the grind and RNG, but even there, a F2P Looter Shooter game, there is better RNG than in MHWilds endgame.
Good fuckin' luck trying to craft AND roll a weapon with good rolls (there are 5 rolls for the base weapon + 2 from the upgrade from the "endgame" monster that you will be fighting over and over again with nothing new until the expansion, which I don't think I'll buy after playing this).
MHWorld had a system like this, but if you got a bad roll on a weapon, you could just reroll the bad roll until you got everything good, unlike MHWilds where if you got a bad roll, the weapon is useless and you have to start again.

I went blind on this game and boy this shit disappointed me, if I had just watched a video about the endgame or looked up how difficult (or how easy) it was, I would've never purchased it.

 MH3U and MHWorld will always be the GOATs.

Oh, and fuck whoever thought giving our hunters (and palicoes even tho you can disable that for them) a voice was a good idea.

Campaign: 3/10 (it's a MH game, the campaing will never be good, but this one is bad)
Combat: 5/10 (too easy, focus mode makes the game easier than what the clutch claws did in MHW Iceborne)
Endg…

citations.review_text: After all the performance updates, I can safely recommend this game.

after a rough first 6 months, Monster Hunter: Wilds finally found its footing and fixed some major issues, and with a fantastic looking dlc on the way, now's the time to jump in, kill some monsters, and make a new hate.

back when the game first launched i could barely run it, but they've optimized the game so much I don't have any problems anymore, and I don't even have an great laptop, so if your worried about performance, I wouldn't worry. besides performance the game itself is addicting, off sets, new move sets, fun monsters, the whole game is great. the game starts off easy because its meant to be easy to warm new comers into the series, but it does ramp up in difficulty so don't worry about it being too easy. over all one of my favorite games, I'd definitely recommend.

single_points.text: One reviewer says it would be cool if the game explained literally anything about how things work and calls it the worst UI they have ever seen in a video game.

citation.review_text: it would be cool if the game explained literally anything about how things work. also the worst UI i've ever seen in a video game. otherwise very fun gameplay and lots of replayability
